summary: DIRECTER introduces a dynamic, plausibility-guided activation steering method that adaptively modulates KV cache scaling strength per decoding step, addressing the oversteering problem that plagues static steering methods. The contribution is genuinely novel and the empirical results are consistent across three benchmarks and five model scales (1B–14B), with strong ablations and efficiency analysis. However, the paper has notable gaps in statistical reporting (no seeds, error bars, or significance tests on main results), a limited set of steering baselines (only PASTA and SpotLight), and an under-validated new benchmark (GSM8K-Format), which together place it in the borderline-accept range pending fixes.
strengths: The core idea of coupling activation steering with a plausibility-guided rejection loop is genuinely novel and addresses a real, well-motivated problem (oversteering) that prior static methods do not solve.

The layer-ranking mechanism via attention sensitivity is a principled, one-time prefill analysis that inverts KV cache quantization logic in an elegant way, and is well-validated by ablations (ranking reversed, random layers, random tokens).

The method preserves generation quality and task fidelity (≈92%, highest among all baselines) while improving instruction following, which is the key practical advantage over PASTA and SpotLight that sacrifice task accuracy.

Strong generalization evidence across model families (Llama, Qwen) and scales (1B–14B), with consistent improvements, plus a thorough efficiency analysis showing only ~16% throughput reduction and negligible memory overhead.
The plausibility filter is shown to be modular and composable, improving other steering methods (PASTA, SpotLight) when used as a safety gate, which adds practical value beyond the standalone method.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical reporting is absent on all main results: Table 1 and Table 2 report single point estimates with no seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Only two ablation rows (random layers, random tokens) show ±variance, making it impossible to assess whether the 6.5% average gain and the smaller cross-model gains (e.g., 61.6 vs 61.3 on Qwen-2.5-3B) are statistically real.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Run at least 3–5 seeds (where stochasticity applies) or report bootstrap confidence intervals over the evaluation set for all main results, and add paired significance tests (e.g., McNemar or bootstrap) against the zero-shot and strongest steering baseline.

key_concerns.issue: The steering baseline set is narrow: only PASTA and SpotLight are compared, both attention-level methods. The related work discusses steering vectors (Turner et al., 2023), representation engineering (Zou et al., 2023), and contrastive-pair methods (Chen et al., 2025), none of which appear in experiments, leaving open whether DIRECTER beats simpler residual-stream steering or contrastive decoding baselines.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one residual-stream / steering-vector baseline and one contrastive-decoding baseline (e.g., CAD or DoLa) on IFEval to demonstrate that the gains are not specific to beating only attention-level steering competitors.

key_concerns.issue: The new benchmark GSM8K-Format is introduced without sufficient validation: the construction procedure is described only briefly and detailed in an appendix not visible here, and there is no inter-annotator agreement, no release commitment, and no comparison to existing formatting-constraint benchmarks, making it hard to judge whether reported gains reflect benchmark artifacts.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Provide full construction details in the main text, report basic reliability statistics, and ideally release the benchmark; also discuss whether the formatting constraints are representative of real-world instruction-following demands.

key_concerns.issue: The 'model-agnostic' claim is supported by only two transformer families (Llama, Qwen) of the same decoder-only architecture; no non-Transformer or alternative-architecture test is included, so the generality claim is slightly overstated.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Soften the 'model-agnostic' wording to 'across tested decoder-only Transformer families' or add at least one architecturally different model.

key_concerns.issue: The LLM-judge evaluation (Table 4) relies solely on gpt-4o-mini, which has known position and length biases; the human evaluation is mentioned but its details (number of annotators, agreement, protocol) are in an appendix not visible here, so the fidelity claim rests largely on an unverified judge.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report human-evaluation protocol and inter-annotator agreement in the main text, and ideally cross-check the LLM judge against a second judge or a held-out human-labeled subset.

key_concerns.issue: Algorithm 2 (full procedure) and several key methodological details (sensitivity metric simplification, span detection) are referenced as being in appendices not visible here, which makes the main-text method section slightly underspecified for independent reproduction of the sensitivity analysis.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Include the essential computation of the sensitivity score and its efficient approximation in the main text so the method is self-contained.

questions_for_authors: What is the variance / statistical significance of the main results in Table 1 and Table 2, and are the smaller gains (e.g., +0.3 on Qwen-2.5-3B) statistically significant?
How does DIRECTER compare to a residual-stream steering-vector baseline or a contrastive-decoding baseline (CAD/DoLa) on IFEval?
How exactly was GSM8K-Format constructed, and what is its reliability (e.g., inter-annotator agreement on the formatting rubric)?
What is the wall-clock cost of the one-time attention sensitivity analysis relative to prefill, and how does it scale with context length?
How sensitive is DIRECTER to the accuracy of the instruction-span detection in real-world prompts where instructions are interleaved with task content?
Were the human annotators for the quality/fidelity evaluation blinded to the method, and what was the inter-annotator agreement?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly well-scoped, but the 'model-agnostic' and 'general-purpose enhancement module' phrasing slightly overgeneralizes from two same-architecture families and three benchmarks; the core instruction-following and quality-preservation claims are, however, well-supported by the evidence presented.

significance.justification: Addresses a real and recognized problem (oversteering in steering methods) with a practical, reusable dynamic-control mechanism that other inference-time methods could adopt, but the absolute gains (~6.5% over zero-shot, ~4% over prior steering) are moderate rather than transformative.

novelty.justification: The integration of KV cache scaling with a per-step plausibility-guided rejection loop and a sensitivity-based layer ranking is a genuinely new combination not present in prior static steering or contrastive decoding work.

rigor.justification: The method is sound, ablations isolate the key design choices, and the claim–evidence link is generally correct, but limited baselines and absent significance testing reduce confidence in the magnitude of the gains.

statistical_soundness.justification: Main tables report single point estimates with no seeds, error bars, or significance tests; only two ablation rows show variance, which is below the rigor bar for an ICLR empirical paper claiming consistent improvements.

calibration_honesty.justification: Most claims are appropriately scoped and limitations (sensitivity metric lacks theory, instruction-span separation assumption) are acknowledged, but 'model-agnostic' and 'general-purpose' phrasing slightly overstates the breadth of the evidence.

clarity.justification: The paper is well-organized and the method is explained clearly with a helpful overview figure and algorithm; some notation (e.g., top-2 token indices) is dense but readable.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard conference structure (Intro, Related Work, Method, Experiments, Conclusion) is followed well, with a reasonable length and clear RQ-driven experimental organization.

reproducibility.justification: Key hyperparameters (α=100, β=0.5) and model choices are stated, but the full sensitivity computation and Algorithm 2 are deferred to appendices, and the new benchmark construction is not self-contained in the main text.

related_work.justification: Prior activation steering and instruction-following work is discussed fairly and the contribution is delineated clearly against PASTA and SpotLight, though several cited steering-vector and contrastive-decoding methods are not carried into the experimental comparison.

figure_quality.justification: Captions are informative and each display item supports a specific claim (overview, ablations, robustness, efficiency), but several tables are dense and the main results table would benefit from variance annotations.

breadth_generality.justification: Only two steering baselines, two same-architecture model families, and one newly introduced benchmark with limited validation, so the claimed generality is under-supported relative to the breadth of prior steering literature.

overall_recommendation.justification: A sound, novel, and useful contribution with consistent empirical support and good ablations, but missing significance testing and a narrow baseline set keep it at borderline-accept pending minor revisions.
